# Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) mode the shared closing (Income → Incident → EndCheck) is presented as a single condensed, text-only summary. The full end-of-turn income choreography that single-player players see — base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD coin collection, with per-card coin grids and sound — never runs for the AI seats (nor for the human seat). Much of the end-of-turn phase is therefore lost in an AI game.

## Users

- **Competitive mode players** (especially the human seat) who want to see the outcome of each player's day — what each seat earned and what effects fired — with the same visual feedback as single-player, rather than an unexplained jump to the next day.
- **Maintainers** who want a single end-of-turn presentation path so the single-player and competitive flows cannot drift.

Example user stories:
- "As a competitive player, after I end my day I want to watch each player's income collection in turn, so I understand how the shared day changed every seat's economy."
- "As a competitive player on a slow machine, I want the AI closing to be short and skippable, so playing against AI does not take many minutes per day."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1: Per-seat full closing presentation (phase-major)** — After the shared competitive closing resolves, the presentation runs the full phased income choreography (`animateIncomePhases`: base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD collection) once as a single **phase-major** sweep over all non-eliminated seats, in seat order: each phase plays for the human seat, then AI 1, then AI 2, before the next phase begins, using each seat's own income/effects. The human seat is included; eliminated seats are skipped. (Amended 2026-10-12 per producer audit 2026-10-08: previously seat-major, one full choreography per seat.)
- **AC2: Authoritative per-seat data** — The competitive closing surfaces the per-owner income (`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `OwnerIncomeResult[]`, which already carries a full `IncomeResult.phaseBreakdown`) instead of discarding it, and every presented per-seat value equals the delta actually applied to that `PlayerRecord` (asserted by test).
- **AC3: Per-seat income feedback text** — The closing summary reports each seat's income (e.g. `Player 2: +7 coins`), not the shared host total, which can differ from any player's actual income.
- **AC4: Shared engine semantics unchanged** — Presentation-only change: the closing order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), the single shared incident per day, and seeded-replay determinism are unchanged.
- **AC5: Single presentation primitive** — Single-player and competitive closings are driven by one shared presentation path; `finishTurnPresentation` and `presentCompetitiveClosing` no longer duplicate the income/incident/end-of-turn/advance logic. Single-player behaviour is behaviourally unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass without modification). This absorbs **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ**.
- **AC6: Bounded and non-blocking** — Full animations run in normal play; reduced motion, replay and headless contexts fall back to per-seat text and always advance the day; the presentation **waits** for the phase-major choreography to finish collecting before the day advances (never leaves it running in the background while the next turn starts), bounded by a global fast-forward cap so a large roster cannot stall the game (honours MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD AC4).
- **AC7: Tests** — New/updated automated tests cover: per-seat animation sequencing (one full choreography per non-eliminated seat, in order), authoritative per-seat values (presented == applied deltas), bounded/headless fallback (day always advances; text-only when animations are disabled), and single-player unchanged.
- **AC8: Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** (producer decision Q2-A): no change to the engine closing order or the shared-incident contract; income/incident still resolve once per shared day.
- **Bounded** (producer decision Q3-A): the closing must never block the day start indefinitely; reduced motion / replay / headless degrade to text.
- **Determinism**: the presentation must not consume RNG or mutate state (beyond reusing the existing deferred-delta window where applicable), so seeded replay stays reproducible.
- **Single-player parity**: single-player end-of-turn presentation and its deferred-mutation flow (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) must not regress.
- Phaser-free helpers where possible, so the node integration tests can exercise the flow (`MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive` is already Phaser-free).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
  - `endCompetitiveTurnDay` → `driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` → `runCompetitiveClosing` → `presentCompetitiveClosing` → `startTurnPhase`.
  - `presentCompetitiveClosing` shows `Resolving end-of-turn effects...`, a one-line `competitiveClosingSummary` built from the **shared** `result.income.total` and the incident name, then `End of turn complete.` after a ~900 ms hold. It deliberately does **not** run `animateIncomePhases` (test `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` asserts `incomeCalls` is empty).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` calls `applyCompetitiveIncome(state)` and **discards** the returned `OwnerIncomeResult[]`; `TurnResult.income` carries only the shared `applyIncome` result. `applyCompetitiveIncome` already builds a per-owner `IncomeResult` with a full `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — single-player `endTurn` delegates to `processEndOfTurn` (with `deferResourceApplication`) then `animateIncomePhases`, then `finishTurnPresentation`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomePhases(animator, phaseData, options)` runs the phased choreography from `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]` (indexed against the shared street grid) and applies `options.pendingDeltas` exactly once at collection completion; `incomeCollectionActive` gates the HUD delta pop.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — the competitive HUD binds each row to that seat's `state.players` coins/reputation/score (so a per-seat collection can land on the right row).
- `MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD` delivered the condensed text-only competitive closing; `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` (open) proposed per-seat income surfacing + presentation dedup and is folded into this item.

## Desired change

After the shared competitive closing resolves, present the results **per seat, in turn**, with full animations:

1. Surface per-owner income/effects from the closing (`OwnerIncomeResult[]`, or an equivalent per-seat breakdown on `TurnResult`) so the presentation has authoritative data.
2. For each non-eliminated seat in seat order, run the full `animateIncomePhases` choreography using that seat's `phaseBreakdown.perSlotBreakdown`, applying that seat's deltas at the appropriate time (reusing the existing deferred-delta window so the HUD updates when the coins land).
3. Show the resolved incident reveal once (unchanged shared semantics) and a per-seat income summary.
4. Extract one shared presentation primitive used by both single-player (`finishTurnPresentation`) and competitive (`presentCompetitiveClosing`); the competitive path iterates seats while single-player presents its single seat — no duplicated logic.
5. Keep it bounded/non-blocking: reduced motion / replay / headless skip animation and show per-seat text; a global fast-forward bound (e.g. per-seat gap reduction or a total-time cap) ensures the day always advances.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — `presentCompetitiveClosing` becomes per-seat; extract a shared primitive; update `competitiveClosingSummary` to per-seat output.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `finishTurnPresentation` consumes the shared primitive (single-seat).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — surface `OwnerIncomeResult[]` from `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (currently discarded); thread it through `TurnResult`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — reuse `animateIncomePhases`; confirm per-seat phase data + per-seat delta application (may need a per-seat `pendingDeltas`/HUD target hook).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `TurnResult` may gain an optional per-seat income field (backwards-compatible; absent for single-player).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — HUD target binding if collection must credit a specific seat row.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` — update/extend (current test asserts the choreography is **not** run; that assertion inverts).
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-*` — reference for per-seat sequencing assertions; `tests/main-street/competitive-income-events.test.ts` for authoritative per-owner income.

## Related work

- **Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)** — this item.
- **Refactor end-of-turn presentation: remove single-player/competitive duplication and add per-seat income feedback (MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ)** — **superseded/absorbed** by this item (producer decision Q1-A); closed as superseded.
- **End Turn Phase is missing in AI game (MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD)** — delivered the condensed text-only competitive closing this item replaces with full per-seat animations.
- **Competitive turn orchestration in the scene (MS-0MUTU8IYV0086PF6)** and **Playable AI competitive mode (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP)** — the competitive turn flow this sits on.
- **Coin and Reputation should count up/down (MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8)** — open; related HUD-counting polish for end-of-turn reconciliation.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — total duration**: full per-seat choreography is ~11 s each; with N seats this could make AI days very long. Mitigation: the bounded requirement (AC6) plus a global fast-forward bound; consider shortening per-seat gaps.
- **Risk — HUD targeting**: the competitive HUD binds per-seat rows; the collection currently assumes the single shared `resourceBank` projection. Mitigation: add a per-seat HUD target to the collection, or animate against the shared HUD only when a single row is present.
- **Risk — deferred-delta window**: competitive closing currently applies deltas before presentation, unlike the single-player deferred path. Mitigation: reuse or extend the existing deferred-delta mechanism so the per-seat values land when each seat's coins collect.
- **Risk — test inversion**: `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` explicitly asserts the full choreography is *not* run; that contract is intentionally inverted here.
- **Assumption**: the presentation is a replay over already-resolved state (per-owner income from `applyCompetitiveIncome`) — no engine-phase change.
- **Assumption**: a per-seat income breakdown is preferable to the shared host total (producer decisions Q1-A/Q2-A).
- **Scope-creep risk**: restyling the HUD, changing the incident system, or adding a player-facing speed toggle are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (relationship to MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ)** — "How should this relate to the per-seat income feedback / presentation-refactor item?" — **Answer (producer): A. Merge/supersede** — this item absorbs the per-seat income feedback AC; MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ is folded in (and closed as superseded). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (engine semantics vs presentation)** — "Should the end-of-turn phase actually run per player in the engine, or should the engine keep the shared closing and only the presentation run per seat?" — **Answer (producer): A. Presentation-only** — keep the shared closing resolved once (shared/street incident semantics, determinism unchanged); replay each seat's economy sequentially with full animations. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (duration / boundedness)** — "Full choreography per seat could take ~11 s each; how should duration be handled?" — **Answer (producer): A. Full choreography per seat, bounded** — full animation normally, global fast-forward bound, and text-only fallback for reduced motion / replay / headless. Source: interactive reply.
- **Research context** (pre-question, recorded for traceability): competitive closing is text-only and discards `applyCompetitiveIncome`'s per-owner results (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`); single-player runs `animateIncomePhases` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`); the competitive HUD binds per-seat rows (`src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts`).
- **Q4 (plan approval)** — "Do you approve the proposed 6-phase, 10-item feature decomposition (test-first), or would you like to edit/split/merge items?" — **Answer (producer): approve as proposed ("LGTM")** — no changes requested. Final: approved. Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUACDDMX004KWY8** – Bank your spare action is a dead end in the tutorial (open)
- **MS-0MURQY8VU002XIQK** – Integration, AI compatibility, and legacy equivalence tests (completed)
- **MS-0MUWE6OER004GNV1** – Full-suite verification and regression (completed)

# Intake Brief: Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships and upgrade chains (MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**
**Producer decisions (2026-10-07, interactive): Q1 = A (docs/tooling artefacts); Q2 = B (named three + community-space extension); Q3 = A (committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard).** See Appendix.

## Problem statement

The repo already generates a deterministic Mermaid flowchart of the storyline
graph (`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`,
with a JSON manifest and a `--check` drift guard), but no other card dataset is
visualised. Designers, reviewers and new contributors must reconstruct card
synergies, staff coverage, upgrade chains and community-space relationships by
reading 174 CSV rows. Generating the same class of deterministic Mermaid
diagram for these datasets makes each relationship legible at a glance and
keeps the pictures drift-guarded against `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Content designer / producer** — sees at a glance which cards share a synergy,
  which staff can serve which businesses, and how upgrade chains branch and gate.
  - *"As a designer, I want a Mermaid diagram of card synergies, so I can check
    that every synergy type has a healthy cluster of cards without reading the CSV."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of staff coverage, so I can spot uncovered
    business types or overly broad staff."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of upgrade chains, so I can see the two-step
    level-1 → level-2 branches and their gates."*
- **Reviewer / balancer** — trusts the committed diagrams because a drift guard
  fails when they fall out of sync with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **New contributor / developer** — uses the diagrams as an entry point to the
  card model, alongside `card-catalog.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Diagram generator CLI.** A new dev-only npm script (e.g. `npm run
   docs:diagrams`) generates Mermaid from `src/card-data.csv` through the typed
   card model under `vite-node`, supporting `--diagram
   <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`), `--format
   mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>` and `--check` (drift guard:
   exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date). Verified by unit tests that invoke
   the CLI and assert its exit codes and output.
2. **Committed artefacts & drift guard.** Four deterministic Mermaid artefacts
   are committed under `docs/main-street/` — `card-synergies.mmd`,
   `staff-relationships.mmd`, `upgrade-chains.mmd`,
   `community-space-relationships.mmd` — and a Vitest drift guard regenerates
   each from `src/card-data.csv` and fails when the committed file differs
   byte-for-byte. The existing `storyline-graph.mmd` drift guard continues to pass.
3. **Card synergy diagram content.** Shows every business and community-space
   card and all six synergy types (Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
   Entertainment, Health), with an edge per card↔synergy membership so cards that
   can chain adjacency bonuses are identifiable. Verified by unit tests asserting
   the exact node set plus edges for representative multi-synergy cards (e.g.
   `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture; `cs-public-art` → Culture + Entertainment) and
   that all six synergy types appear.
4. **Staff relationship diagram content.** Shows every staff card, each synergy
   type and named business it may serve (`allowedBusinessTypes`, resolved through
   the existing `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`
   helpers), and the specialization-skill catalog from `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`
   (categories and skills). Verified by unit tests asserting representative staff
   edges (e.g. `staff-health-safety` → Health only; `staff-chef` →
   Cafe/Diner/Delicatessen/Food) and that every catalog skill appears.
5. **Upgrade chain diagram content.** Shows each upgradeable business/community
   space as a chain root plus each applicable upgrade, ordered by
   `requiredLevel`/`maxLevel` and labelled with `newDisplayName`, so level-1
   branches and the level-2 gate are visible. Verified by unit tests asserting the
   four level-2 chains (e.g. Bakery → Patisserie / Bread Factory → Grand
   Bakehouse) and that a level-2 upgrade is only shown after a level-1 step.
6. **Community-space diagram content.** Shows each of the eight community-space
   cards, its synergy types and any community-space upgrade (`targetBusiness`),
   including ongoing cost/buff fields where set. Verified by unit tests asserting
   all eight cards and their types.
7. **Determinism & safety.** Two builds from the same CSV are deeply equal, output
   is sorted and contains no timestamp/RNG/wall-clock input, the generator adds no
   runtime dependency (dev tooling only), and Mermaid remains the source of truth
   (artefacts are never hand-edited). Verified by unit tests.
8. **Documentation.** A new `docs/main-street/card-diagrams.md` documents every
   diagram (what it shows, how to read it) and the regeneration command, and
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   `src/README.md` link to it. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
9. **Tests, build and full suite.** `npm run build` succeeds and the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mermaid is the source of truth.** The committed `.mmd` files are generated
  artefacts; never hand-edited. `src/card-data.csv` is the data source.
- **No new runtime dependency.** The generator is dev tooling only, mirroring
  `storylines:graph`; nothing enters the game bundle.
- **Determinism.** Sorted node/edge order, no RNG, timestamps or wall-clock input;
  byte-identical on re-run.
- **Read-only over data.** Do not change the card model, CSV schema/column order,
  or gameplay data; consume the existing typed getters
  (`getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getUpgradeTemplates`,
  `getStaffCardTemplates`) and `MainStreetStaffSkills`.
- **Rendering is out of scope.** SVG/PNG rendering of Mermaid stays with
  `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`; this item commits `.mmd` (and offers `--format json` on
  demand only).
- **Scope guard.** Additional diagram domains beyond the four named (plus the
  already-existing storyline graph) are separate work items; record them rather
  than absorbing them here.
- **UK English** in all generated labels and documentation.
- **No CHANGELOG.md edits** (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state (repo research)

- **Generator precedent.** `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` builds a
  deterministic manifest and renders Mermaid; `src/scripts/storyline-graph-cli.ts`
  is the `vite-node` entry (`npm run storylines:graph`); `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`
  holds the existing byte-for-byte drift guard.
- **Typed getters.** `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` exposes
  `getBusinessTemplates`, `getCommunitySpaceTemplates`, `getEventTemplates`,
  `getUpgradeTemplates`, `getStaffCardTemplates` (re-exported via
  `src/MainStreetCards.ts`).
- **Data.** `src/card-data.csv` — 174 rows: 31 business, 39 upgrade, 25 staff,
  8 community-space, 71 event. Synergy types: Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
  Entertainment, Health.
- **Synergies.** `BusinessCard`/`CommunitySpaceCard` carry `synergyTypes`,
  `synergyCoinBonus`, `synergyRepBonus`; staff `skill-network`/`skill-tech-guru`
  modify adjacency behaviour.
- **Staff.** `staff.allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types and specific
  business names (e.g. `Cafe|Diner|Food|Delicatessen`); resolved by
  `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`. Specialization
  skills live in `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` (category + effect).
- **Upgrades.** `upgrade.targetBusiness` + `upgrade.requiredLevel` + business
  `maxLevel`; `upgrade.newDisplayName` names the upgraded form. Four level-2
  upgrades gate on a level-1 parent (`upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`,
  `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat`).
- **Community spaces.** Eight cards with `synergyTypes` and community-space
  upgrades (e.g. `upg-orchard` → Community Garden).
- **Docs.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` catalogues cards; `storylines.md`
  documents the storyline graph tooling and links `storyline-graph.mmd`;
  `src/README.md` references the scripts; there is **no** `card-diagrams.md` and
  no diagram for synergies/staff/upgrades/community spaces.

## Desired change

1. Add a deterministic diagram generator (`src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` + CLI)
   that builds, for the four domains, a node/edge manifest from the typed card
   model and renders Mermaid, reusing the storyline-graph conventions
   (deterministic ordering, `--check`, `--format`, `--out`).
2. Commit the four `.mmd` artefacts under `docs/main-street/`.
3. Add an npm script (`docs:diagrams`) and a Vitest drift guard for each
   artefact.
4. Document the diagrams and the regeneration workflow, and cross-link from
   `card-catalog.md`, `storylines.md` and `src/README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/card-diagrams.ts` — **new**: manifest builders and Mermaid renderers for synergies, staff, upgrades and community spaces (deterministic; mirrors `storyline-graph.ts`).
- `src/scripts/card-diagrams-cli.ts` — **new** `vite-node` CLI entry with `--diagram`, `--format`, `--out`, `--check`.
- `package.json` — add the `docs:diagrams` script.
- `docs/main-street/card-synergies.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/staff-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/upgrade-chains.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/community-space-relationships.mmd` — **new** committed artefact.
- `docs/main-street/card-diagrams.md` — **new**: diagram guide + regeneration commands.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — link the diagrams.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — cross-reference the unified diagram tooling (§5/§11).
- `src/README.md` — document the new script and artefacts.
- `tests/main-street/card-diagrams.test.ts` — **new**: determinism, content-correctness and drift-guard tests.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — read-only reuse of the typed getters.
- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — read-only specialization-skill catalog source.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed) — the generator/drift-guard pattern this item mirrors.
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open) — owns Mermaid→SVG rendering; out of scope here.
- **MS-0MUYK064P0032374** — Static docs site that renders Mermaid docs at build time (open) — a future rendering surface for these artefacts.
- **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** — Visual storyline authoring editor (open, epic) — an interactive graph viewer; potential consumer of the diagram model.
- **MS-0MUMP968H005MXZY** — Canonical docs, cross-references & doc-drift guard (completed) — docs conventions this item follows.
- **MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN** — Synergy tooltop (completed) — established synergy-type player-facing semantics.
- **MS-0MUR9INHX001QCSE** — Track synergy diversity (G4/HHI) and placement dominance post-rebalance (open) — analytical use of the same synergy data.
- **MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4** — Level-2 upgrade prerequisite gate blocks expensive-tier adoption in greedy Monte Carlo (in-progress) — the level gate visualised in the upgrade chain diagram.

### Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MULWEEE8007J2TB** – Fix Accountant refreshCostDiscount value to ×100 scale (completed)
- **MS-0MTIIKVJE006GRQY** – Competitive state model: per-player resources, owner-tagged street (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: chains, synergies, staff, upgrades, requiredlevel, maxlevel, specialization (+26 more)
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+35 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: diagram, generate, graph, manifest, card, staff, upgrades (+31 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (MEDIUM).** "Any other sensible information" invites unbounded diagrams. *Mitigation:* fix the set at the four named domains plus the existing storyline graph; extra domains become separate work items.
- **Diagram readability (MEDIUM).** A 31-business synergy graph can become dense. *Mitigation:* group by synergy type (central type nodes), keep labels compact (name + id), and offer `--diagram` for per-domain output.
- **Upgrade-chain modelling (MEDIUM).** `requiredLevel` + `maxLevel` encode a graph that can branch (Bakery has two level-1 options and one level-2). *Mitigation:* model chains by `targetBusiness` + `requiredLevel`, assert the four level-2 chains explicitly in tests.
- **Staff target ambiguity (LOW).** `allowedBusinessTypes` mixes synergy types with business names. *Mitigation:* resolve through the existing helpers and distinguish node kinds in the diagram/tests.
- **Drift staleness (LOW).** Committed diagrams can diverge from the CSV. *Mitigation:* per-artefact `--check` drift guard.
- **Assumption** — "diagrams" means committed Mermaid artefacts in the docs, not an in-game viewer (Q1 = A).
- **Assumption** — the four named domains plus the community-space extension are the v1 set (Q2 = B).
- **Assumption** — `.mmd` is committed and drift-guarded; `--format json` is available on demand but not committed (Q3 = A).
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface: where do the diagrams live?** Options: (A) docs/tooling artefacts (committed `.mmd` under `docs/main-street/`, mirroring `storylines:graph`); (B) in-game player-facing Mermaid viewer; (C) both. **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — docs/tooling artefacts. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Diagram scope.** Options: (A) the three named domains only; (B) A plus a curated extension (community-space relationships and other clearly diagram-worthy data); (C) a single combined "everything" diagram. **Recommended: (B).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (B)** — named three plus the community-space extension. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Output and guarding.** Options: (A) deterministic committed `.mmd` plus a `--check` drift guard per diagram; (B) on-demand only, no committed artefacts or guard; (C) A plus rendered SVG/PNG (overlaps `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`). **Recommended: (A).** **Answer (producer, 2026-10-07): (A)** — committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard; SVG rendering stays with `MS-0MUNB54KU005084C`. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent, no producer input needed): the storyline generator
(`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts`) is the established pattern (`--format`,
`--out`, `--check`, deterministic ordering, committed artefact + drift test);
the typed template getters for business/community-space/upgrade/staff already
exist; and no synergy/staff/upgrade/community-space diagram exists today.

## Goal

Track the residual below-target expensive-tier upgrades left after MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M.

## Context

discovered-from:MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M. On the canonical `mc-balance` Medium profile (200 seeds, 60 turns, greedy), the branching level-0 prerequisites `upg-drive-in` (cost 700) and `upg-wellness-center` (cost 900) remain at/near 0% M1 because they compete for the single upgrade market slot with the standard path (`upg-imax`, `upg-resort-spa`) weighted by MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W. Raising their `drawWeight` lifted them but nudged the level-2 capstone `upg-luxury-retreat` below 5%, so MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M left them unchanged rather than over-tune the market.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Canonical before/after Monte Carlo evidence (200 seeds, `mc-balance`, 60 turns, greedy Easy/Medium/Hard) records M1 for `upg-drive-in` and `upg-wellness-center`.
2. A card-data-only change (cost/`incomeBonus`/`drawWeight`) lifts both to >=5% M1 on Medium without regressing the four level-2 capstones below 5% and without breaking the Easy >= Medium >= Hard win-rate ladder.
3. Full test suite passes.

## Constraints

Card data only; no engine-rule change. If unreachable, document the shortfall and escalate separately.

# Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import

**Headline:** Ship a real, production residential-themed card pack (~10 balanced
cards with bespoke art) for Main Street, gated behind the launcher's unified
content-unlock store, with a scoped simulated-purchase flow that proves the
end-to-end pack **unlock → import** path.

## Problem statement

The card-pack DLC channel (merge, persistence and in-game listing) has shipped,
but there is no real Main Street pack exercising the **unlock → import** path
end-to-end, and no pack gated by the launcher's unified content-unlock store.
Without committed pack content plus a simulated purchase, the DLC feature cannot
be demonstrated or regression-tested beyond in-memory stubs.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — unlocks the residential pack and sees its new cards
  dealt into play.
  - *As a player, I want to buy/unlock a residential card pack and have its
    cards appear in my pool, so new content extends the game.*
  - *As a player, I want a locked pack to stay out of play until I own it, so
    gated content is respected.*
- **Developer / QA** — uses the simulated purchase to verify the whole channel.
  - *As a QA engineer, I want to simulate a pack purchase without a real
    storefront, so I can test lock → unlock → enable → deal → save/load.*
- **Producer** — demonstrates the DLC channel with real, shippable content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A production pack source tree exists under a new top-level `packs/` directory
   (`manifest.json` + `main-street/main-street-residential-pack/` CSV fragment +
   art), reuses Main Street's `card-data.csv` header **exactly**, has unique card
   ids, and builds cleanly with the core card-pack builder into an installable
   `<contentDir>/packs/` root.
2. The pack adds roughly ten new **residential-themed** cards spanning the
   families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space); each row follows
   the existing tier/cost/effect conventions and the set passes the
   balance/catalogue checks.
3. Every new card has bespoke project-generated art in `src/sprites/` and
   resolves to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art through the regenerated
   `card-art-map.json`.
4. The pack is gated on the unified content-unlock store: while locked its cards
   stay out of play; a scoped simulated purchase (no collateral unlock, state
   persists across restarts) makes it show as unlocked in the Card Packs
   listing, enable-able, merged into the pool, and its cards deal in play.
5. Saves that record the active residential pack restore the same pool on load,
   and a missing/disabled pack degrades gracefully (warn, base content).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Test Plan

- **Unit / content** — pack manifest + CSV validity (exact base header, unique
  ids, family coverage), and balance/catalogue checks over the new rows.
- **Unit / pipeline** — pack gate resolves the pack as locked with no unlock and
  as entitled once a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock
  exists; `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merges the residential rows and the pool
  applies; save/load round-trips the active pack + merged checksum; missing-pack
  degradation.
- **Unit / unlock scope** — the simulated purchase unlocks only the residential
  pack and does **not** unlock the configured itch.io golf reward.
- **Browser / UI** — the Card Packs listing shows the pack locked, the simulated
  purchase flips it to unlocked, and it can then be enabled.
- **Art** — the runtime resolver and the static SVG generator agree that each
  new card resolves to dedicated art (mirrors the existing art-agreement test).

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo surface.** The Main Street pack gate can consume the unified
  store through the existing `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam
  (Main Street side), but the *write* path (a reward rule/verifier simulating the
  purchase) lives in the core launcher. Any core change must be committed to the
  `./core` submodule and the submodule bumped in the same work-item, as previous
  cross-repo items did.
- **Global attestation side effect.** `contentUnlocks.refresh({ attested: true })`
  self-attests *every* configured rule, which would also unlock the itch.io golf
  reward. The simulated purchase must scope verification to the residential pack
  (a `(platform, action)`-keyed verifier or equivalent rule-scoped mechanism).
- **Pack merge rules.** The fragment must reuse the base header exactly;
  duplicate ids or a mismatched header reject the pack whole (core contract).
- **Art.** Art must be project-generated, deterministic/reproducible, and
  licence-clean (CC0 / in-house), matching the existing 1024×1024 source-sprite
  pipeline.
- **Additive only.** No changes to base card data or balance; the pack is purely
  additive.
- **Push policy.** Commit/push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Existing state

- Card-pack channel complete and shipped: `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
  (merge/persistence, one entry point), `MS-0MV07GNUU005E536`; listing UI/boot
  wiring, `MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H`; e2e pipeline test, `MS-0MV0Q479I002W0R6`; docs
  cross-reference, `MS-0MV0R1H5S007TTVG`.
- Core pack contract/loader/merge/entitlement and the reference pack live under
  `core/`: `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts`,
  `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` (with a `resolveEntitlement` seam),
  `core/electron/card-pack-entitlements.ts` (Steam-DLC shaped) and
  `core/tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/` (3-card
  `main-street-foundations`).
- Unified content-unlock store shipped in core: `core/electron/action-rewards.ts`
  (+ `FileContentUnlockStore`), `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts`,
  `core/electron/action-rewards.json`, renderer read client
  `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`, and the pure gate
  `core/src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts`.
- The card-pack gate does **not** currently consult `contentUnlocks`; the loader
  resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC-shaped `cardPackClient`
  (`entitlement.steamAppId` / the DLC catalog placeholder
  `main-street-founders-pack → app 480`).
- Card art is a generated build artefact:
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` builds `src/card-art-map.json`
  from `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` + `src/card-data.csv`.
- `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs` (core `build:card-pack` npm script) turns a
  pack source tree into an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root.

## Desired change

1. **Pack content** — author a new production pack source tree under `packs/`:
   `packs/manifest.json` declaring `main-street-residential-pack`
   (`gameId: main-street`, version, `coreEngineVersion`, `cards`, `assets`);
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` with ~10
   residential-theme cards in the base schema; and
   `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/*.png` pack art. Add a
   Main Street npm script wrapper for the core builder so the build is
   reproducible, and install under `<contentDir>/packs/`.
2. **Art** — generate bespoke 1024×1024 source sprites for the new cards into
   `src/sprites/`, regenerate `src/card-art-map.json`, and (if needed) extend the
   art generator so pack cards are mapped/covered.
3. **Unlock gate** — compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a
   `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` content-unlock (via
   `contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) entitles the pack in addition to the existing
   Steam-DLC status.
4. **Simulated purchase** — add a scoped simulated-purchase reward rule/verifier
   in the core launcher targeting that DLC id, and a dev/QA affordance (for
   example a control in the Card Packs listing) that performs the purchase and
   refreshes the pack pool.
5. **Tests + docs** — cover content validity, the unlock/import pipeline and the
   listing behaviour (per Test Plan); update `README.md`, `src/README.md`,
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and add a pack `README.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which is the target pack artefact and where should its content live —
  (A) a new `main-street-residential-pack` under the reference fixture, (B)

  content under a new top-level `packs/` directory**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "How should the simulated payment work — (A) a dev-only Unlock/Buy

  existing contentUnlocks mechanism**. Research: the pack gate
  (`core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts`) resolves entitlement through the Steam-DLC
  shaped `cardPackClient` and does **not** consult `contentUnlocks`; the

- Q (round 2): "Describe the differences/pros/cons of the content-unlock (C)

## Out of scope

## Plan: changelog

Pre-check decision `plan` (effort Medium, risk High); approval gate **not** required (only Extra-Large effort **and** High/Severe risk pause for producer approval). - **AC2** (~10 residential cards across families, balance/catalogue) → F4 + T1.
- **AC3** (bespoke art in `src/sprites/`, dedicated non-`Fallback` map) → F5 + T2.
- **AC4** (gated on the unified content-unlock store; scoped simulated purchase; listing; deal in play) → F6, F7, F8 + T3.
- **AC5** (save/load restores the pack; missing/disabled degrades) → F6 + T3.
- **AC6** (all related documentation) → D9.
- **AC7** (full suite passes) → T10.

### Phasing

Implemented as independently verifiable slices: content/build → art → gate → scoped purchase → listing → docs → full-suite verification. Each slice carries its own automated coverage; the three `Verification:` children are the dedicated acceptance suites for content/builder, art coverage, and the unlock/purchase/save-load pipeline. Between phases, re-read the next child's description and update it with anything learned (the plan is intentionally a living artefact until each child is implemented).

No new clarifying questions were asked: the intake Appendix above already resolves the pack-location question (C — production content under a new top-level `packs/`), the simulated-payment question (C — reuse the existing `contentUnlocks` mechanism) and the card-set-scope question (B — balance-tuned set, bespoke generated art, ~10 cards). The plan therefore re-uses those answers and records the following documented assumptions and design decisions rather than re-asking:

- **Gating declaration.** The residential pack is gated on the launcher's unified content-unlock store. The read side composes a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock at the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam *in addition to* the existing Steam-DLC status. Which packs are content-unlock gated is a data-driven declaration (proposed: an additive entitlement marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`, parsed by the core manifest/loader). A simpler equivalent that preserves the same behaviour is acceptable — the implementer records the final shape in the work item.

This is the "equivalent rule-scoped mechanism" that prevents `refresh({ attested: true })` from collateral-unlocking anything, and prevents the scoped purchase from unlocking the `itchio-follow` golf reward.

# GitHub Pages Deploy Fails — Playwright Browsers Missing in CI

## Problem

The `Deploy to GitHub Pages` workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) failed at the `npm test` step. `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` uses Playwright's `chromium.launch()` but the CI runner did not have the Playwright Chromium binary installed.

**Symptom:** Live GitHub Pages site was not updated to v0.1.19.

## Root Cause

- `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` is in the `unit` vitest project (not `browser`).
- It imports `renderMermaidBatch`, which calls `chromium.launch()` — the Playwright Chromium binary is required.
- `deploy.yml` did not run `npx playwright install chromium` before `npm test`.
- The Pages workflow triggers only on push to `main`, so the ship skill's PR status-check lookup found nothing.

## Fix

Added an `Install Playwright browsers` step (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`) between `npm ci` and `npm test` in `deploy.yml`, plus a config-contract regression test.

## Evidence

- CI run: 37913849651 — Test step failed with `browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist`
- 5283/5284 tests passed; only this one test was affected.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The GitHub Pages deploy workflow installs Playwright Chromium before the test gate, so `storyline-graph-svg.test.ts` can launch Chromium in CI.
2. A regression test in `tests/deploy/deploy-workflow.test.ts` pins the Playwright install step, the `chromium` target, and its ordering before the `Test` step (fails without the fix).
3. The full unit suite (`npm test`) passes in the worktree.

# Turn log no longer displays

**Regression:** the in-game **Activity Log** panel ("turn log") no longer displays its
entries.

## Problem statement

Players can no longer see the Activity Log panel content, so they lose the running
record of each turn's income, incidents and actions. This is a regression on `dev`
(v0.1.19) and is filed as `critical`.

## Users

- **Main Street players (single-player)** — need the per-turn record to understand
  what happened each turn.
- **Tutorial players** — rely on the log feedback while learning the loop.
- **Competitive players** — need the per-seat action transcript.

Example user stories:

- As a single-player, I want the Activity Log to show each turn's entries as they
  happen, so that I can follow the state of the game.
- As a tutorial player, I want the log to remain visible while the tutorial runs, so
  that I can connect tutorial actions to their outcomes.
- As a competitive player, I want the log to show both seats' actions, so that I can
  follow an AI-vs-AI or mixed match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Activity Log panel renders its entries when the scene loads and updates after each turn completes, in **single-player, tutorial and competitive** modes.
- A new automated test reproduces the blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and passes after the fix (browser test preferred; supplement with unit coverage where the timing contract is involved). The introducing commit is identified (e.g. via `git bisect` or commit-diff inspection) and the fix restores the pre-regression behaviour without changing documented log content or order.
- The two currently-failing tests in `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` (deferral window) pass; their assertion helper must read Phaser `Text.text` correctly (it currently reads `c.text?.text`, which is always `undefined`).
- The deferred-rendering contract is preserved: entries accumulated during end-of-turn closing still appear **after** the upcoming/phase UI, never before it (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Log scrolling/auto-scroll behaviour is unchanged (auto-scroll to newest, no yank when the player has scrolled up).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (unit plus the browser project, run explicitly).

## Constraints

- Must not break the deferred log-render ordering contract (MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2).
- Keep positioning SLL-driven (`src/layouts/main-street.layout.json`); no hard-coded
  pixel coordinates.
- The Phaser/browser context is shared and sensitive: browser tests run serially.
- CI (`npm test`) runs **only** the `unit` Vitest project; `*.browser.test.ts` files
  are excluded. Any browser-level regression coverage must be run explicitly via
  `npx vitest run --project browser` and should be noted as such.

## Existing state

- The Activity Log panel is created once in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (title text `Activity Log`).
- Content is rendered by `refreshLog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, which
  is called from `refreshAll`.
- Deferred rendering is gated by `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`, set/cleared in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`
  (`finishTurnPresentation` / `finalizeTurn` → `flushDeferredLog`).
- Log panel state is reset on scene restart in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`.
- On `dev` HEAD (`b3a9941`):
  - `tests/main-street/activity-log.test.ts` (42 tests) and
    `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` (6 tests) **pass**.
  - `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
    → **2 failed | 15 passed** (re-confirmed by the intake session). The failing cases
    are the deferral-window tests ("suppresses new entry rendering while
    `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete` is set" and "keeps accumulated entries in order
    when rendered after the deferral window"); the failures are caused by the
    assertion helper reading `c.text?.text` (always `undefined` for a Phaser `Text`,
    whose rendered string is the `.text` property itself), which means this browser
    coverage never actually verified the rendered text.
  - Note: `npm test` runs only the `unit` project, so these browser failures do not
    appear in the default suite.

## Desired change

Restore the Activity Log display and make the regression detectable:

1. Identify and fix the root cause of the blank/missing log (prime suspects: the
   deferred-rendering gate never being lifted on some path, or a recent boot/turn-flow
   change on `dev`).
2. Correct the deferral-window browser test helper so it reads the rendered text
   correctly, and add explicit coverage that the log is non-empty on scene load and
   after a turn in each mode.
3. Keep deferral ordering and scroll behaviour intact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — `refreshLog` deferral gate, entry rendering
  and scroll bounds; likely fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — sets/clears
  `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`; verify every path flushes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — log state fields (`logPrevEntryCount`,
  `logAutoScroll`, `logScrollOffset`, …) and `refreshLog` wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Activity Log panel creation.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — log state reset on restart.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts` — fix helper; add
  blank-log regression test.
- `tests/main-street/activity-log-deferred-rendering.test.ts` — deferral timing
  coverage (unit).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed by producer):** "turn log" means the in-game Activity Log
  panel — the only in-game log that lists per-turn entries. The panel and its title
  bar are visible, but the content area is empty and never fills.
- **Risk:** the symptom may only reproduce in the packaged Electron build or a
  specific mode; confirm repro before assuming the fix site.
- **Risk:** fixing the stale browser assertions may reveal the deferral gate really is
  left set on a path not covered by the unit suite.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a log UI redesign is out of scope; record extra ideas as
  linked work items.
- **Risk:** CI does not run browser tests, so a browser-only regression can recur;
  note explicit browser-run expectation in the fix.

## Related work

### Directly related (context / possible cause)

- **MS-0MURBOD2E009SOM2** – Activity Log should not show log line until the results
  have been shown in the UI (completed). Introduced the `logDeferredUntilPhaseComplete`
  gate and the deferral-window browser tests.
- **MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P** – fire banking hint during the tutorial (gate flip + dead-end
  fix) (most recent functional commit on `dev`; touched the turn flow).
- **MS-0MV0OK0XU0062E0H** – Main Street pack listing UI & boot wiring (changed renderer
  and boot).
- **MS-0MV031AYI007UZ7X** – boot/New Game selector ordering
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`, `MainStreetScene.ts`).
- **MS-0MV0319OC002H15F** – Reorder tutorial-offer boot flow.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04** – Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (open)
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed)
- **MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2** – Pedestrians seek the nearest occupied cell (including mid-turn fills) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+248 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, action, actions, actually, add (+211 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: action, actions, activity, actually, add (+173 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Which surface is "the turn log"? Options: (A) whole panel missing; (B)
  panel/title show but content empty/never updates; (C) turn-specific rows
  missing; (D) other.
  — Answer (operator): **B** — the panel and title show, but the content area is
  empty and never updates. Source: interactive reply (intake session
  `herdr-1791559913-2763730-24821`).
- Q: Where and in which mode is it broken? Options: (A) single-player only; (B)
  competitive only; (C) all modes; (D) not sure.
  — Answer (operator): **C** — all modes. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: What is the visible trigger and when did it last work? Options: (A) broken
  from the first turn / on a fresh game; (B) stops after the first End Turn; (C)
  only after loading a save; (D) only under tutorial / reduced-motion; (E) not
  sure.
  — Answer (operator): **A** — broken from the very first turn / on a fresh
  game; described as a "very recent break". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Does the blank log reproduce in the automated suite? — Research (intake
  session, `dev` HEAD `b3a9941`): `npm test` (unit project) **passes**; the
  explicit browser run
  `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/activity-log-rendering.browser.test.ts`
  → **2 failed | 15 passed**, but both failures stem from the stale assertion
  helper (`c.text?.text`), so the suite neither proves nor disproves the
  producer-reported blank log. Source: local run; see "Existing state".

> **Prior-session note:** an earlier intake run (`herdr-1791560667-2819121-4932`)
> drafted this brief but left the three questions above as OPEN QUESTIONs and set
> `needsProducerReview=true`. The producer has now answered them; this appendix
> supersedes those OPEN QUESTIONs.

### Plan session (herdr-1791566842-3344279-31129)

- Q: Are new clarifying questions needed to decompose this work item?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The intake Appendix answers (surface = panel/
  title visible with empty content; scope = all modes; trigger = broken from the
  first turn on a fresh game) already scope the plan, so no new producer questions
  were raised. Source: intake Appendix above; agent reasoning.
- Q: Is a producer plan-approval gate required?
  — Answer (plan, agent): **No.** The effort/risk pre-check returned
  `decision: "plan"` (effort Small, risk High) and the approval gate returned
  `request_approval: false` — approval is only requested for Extra Large effort
  **and** High/Severe risk. Source: `plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed` and
  `plan-approval-gate`.
- Q: Why is the regression test created before the fix?
  — Answer (plan, agent): the AC requires an automated test that reproduces the
  blank-log failure on the pre-fix revision and the introducing commit to be
  identified; the fix depends on that diagnosis. Source: parent AC2/AC3.

> **Plan-session decision (formatting):** the parent Acceptance Criteria list was
> reformatted from a numbered multi-line list to single-line markdown bullets so
> the shared AC-coverage and audit tooling (which parses `- ` bullets) can verify
> coverage. Wording and intent are unchanged.
>
> **Known gap (OPEN QUESTION for the implementing agent):** an automated browser
> repro of the producer-reported blank log has not yet been demonstrated — the
> browser harness logs `Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method
> is not supported in WebGL`, and the existing browser log test passes. The
> test-first child work item must pin the introducing commit before the fix
> child is started. Directed to: the implementing agent; why it matters: the
> fix must target the true root cause, not the stale assertion helper alone.

**Summary:** Author the automated verification that the production residential pack source tree, its CSV fragment and the builder output satisfy the pack contract and the balance/catalogue checks.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read the real authored pack tree (`packs/manifest.json`, `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv`) — not fixtures.
- Drive the real core builder (`core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs`) and the real merge seam (`mergeCardPackCsv`).
- Assert the content is shippable and additive; this item authors tests only (no game code).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Vitest unit suite parses `packs/manifest.json` and asserts it declares the `main-street-residential-pack` entry with `gameId: main-street`, a version, a `coreEngineVersion` range, a `cards` path and its `assets`.
- The suite asserts the pack CSV header equals Main Street's `src/card-data.csv` header **exactly** (same columns, same order), that every new card id is unique, and that no new id/name collides with the base pool.
- The suite asserts the pack adds 8–12 residential-themed cards spanning the families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space) and that the rows follow the existing tier/cost/effect conventions.
- The suite runs `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs --input packs` into a temp directory and asserts the emitted `<out>/manifest.json` + `<out>/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` parse and merge with the base pool via `mergeCardPackCsv` with **no conflicts and no errors**.
- The suite runs the existing schema/balance/catalogue checks over `base + pack` rows and asserts they pass (no invented balance requirements).
- The suite is expected to be red until the pack-content child lands, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackContent.test.ts`.
- Reuse the header/CSV parsing helpers already exercised by `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts`; import the core builder through the `@core-scripts/*` alias.
- Materialise builder output in an `os.tmpdir()` directory and clean up in `afterEach`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackContent.test.ts` — New.
- `packs/manifest.json`, `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` — Read (authored by the pack-content child).
- `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs`, `core/src/core-engine/CardPackMerge.ts`, `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts` — Read.
- `src/card-data.csv` — Base header/id source of truth.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Production residential pack content & builder wrapper** (verifies its output).
- No new production code beyond the test file.

## Deliverables

- A committed, green (after the content child) verification suite and the documented command to run it.

# Verification: residential pack art coverage

**Summary:** Author the automated verification that every residential pack card resolves to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) bespoke art in `src/sprites/` through the regenerated `card-art-map.json`, and that the runtime and static art paths agree.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read the real pack CSV card names and the real committed `src/sprites/` + `src/card-art-map.json`.
- Mirror the existing art-agreement coverage in `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts`.
- Tests only; no game code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Vitest suite derives every distinct card name from the residential pack CSV and asserts `hasDedicatedCardArt(name) === true` and `resolveCardArtName(name) !== CARD_ART_FALLBACK` for each.
- The suite asserts each pack card's intended sprite has a committed `src/sprites/<Sprite>_1024_x_1024.png` source and a bitmap entry in `src/card-art-map.json` with the expected 256×256 WebP resolution/format.
- The suite asserts the runtime resolver (`src/MainStreetCardArt.ts`) and the static SVG generator (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` `resolveCardArtDataUri`) resolve each pack card to the **same** non-Fallback sprite (art-agreement guard).
- The suite asserts the pre-existing base-card art coverage/aliases are unchanged (no regression/churn from regeneration).
- The suite is expected to be red until the pack-art child lands, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackArt.test.ts`, reusing the CSV-name and embedded-bitmap helpers from `card-art.test.ts`.
- Resolve the pack CSV path from a single shared constant/helper so the content and art suites cannot drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackArt.test.ts` — New.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — Pattern source (read).
- `src/MainStreetCardArt.ts`, `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/` — Read.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — Read.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage** (verifies its output).

## Deliverables

- A committed, green (after the art child) verification suite and the documented command to run it.

# Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline

**Summary:** Author the end-to-end verification that a locked residential pack stays out of play, a scoped simulated purchase unlocks **only** it, the pack merges and deals, saves round-trip it, and a missing/disabled pack degrades gracefully — including the browser-level listing behaviour.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Extend the real-content-directory pipeline pattern from `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts` to the production pack.
- Drive the real core action-reward service/store with an in-memory store (no Electron).
- Cover both unit (Node/Vitest) and browser (Chromium) layers; browser files run under the `browser` Vitest project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit suite materialises the production pack into a temp `<contentDir>/packs/` and asserts the gate is **locked** when no `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock exists, and that the pack's card ids are absent from the merged pool and live templates.
- The suite asserts a scoped simulated purchase (the configured dev/QA rule requesting only the residential target) flips the pack to **unlocked**, that it can then be enabled, and that its card ids appear in the merged pool and are dealt by the game.
- The suite asserts the scoped purchase unlocks **only** the residential pack and does **not** unlock the configured itch.io golf reward (`itchio-follow`), and that a global `refresh({ attested: true })` does not unlock the residential pack.
- The suite asserts save → reset → load round-trips the active residential pack, the merged pool checksum and the cards in play, and that a missing/disabled pack degrades to base content with a warning (refusing to resume only when a live instance needs a missing template).
- A browser suite asserts the Card Packs listing shows the residential pack **locked**, the simulated-purchase control flips it to **unlocked**, and it is then enable-able.
- The suites are expected to be red until the gate, purchase and listing children land, then green with no further test edits.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts` (unit) extending the existing pipeline helpers.
- New `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPurchase.browser.test.ts` (browser) mirroring `CardPackListing.browser.test.ts`.
- Inject a deterministic `ContentUnlockClient`/bridge fake plus the real `ActionRewardService` wired to the residential purchase rule so scoping is proven without the launcher.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts` — New.
- `tests/main-street/ResidentialPackPurchase.browser.test.ts` — New.
- `tests/main-street/CardPackPipelineIntegration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/CardPackListing.browser.test.ts` — Pattern source (read).
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Read.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.ts`, `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts`, `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — Read.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Production residential pack content & builder wrapper**, **Content-unlock pack entitlement gate**, **Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher** and **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance**.

## Deliverables

- Committed unit + browser verification suites, green once the dependent children land, with the documented run commands.

# Production residential pack content & builder wrapper

**Summary:** Author the shipped production residential card pack under a new top-level `packs/` directory and wire a Main Street npm wrapper around the core card-pack builder so it builds reproducibly into an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- New production content only; purely additive (no base `card-data.csv` or balance changes).
- Pack id / DLC id: `main-street-residential-pack`; `gameId`: `main-street`.
- Reuse the core pack contract, builder and merge seam — no bespoke build logic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `packs/manifest.json` declares the `main-street-residential-pack` entry (`gameId: main-street`, version, `coreEngineVersion` range, `cards`, `assets`) alongside the reference pack catalogue shape.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` reuses Main Street's `src/card-data.csv` header **exactly** and adds 8–12 residential-themed cards spanning the families (business, event, upgrade, staff, community-space), with unique ids and no id/name collision with the base pool; rows follow the existing tier/cost/effect conventions.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` contains the pack art assets, and `packs/README.md` documents authoring, building and installing the pack.
- `package.json` gains a `build:card-pack` wrapper invoking `core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs --input packs`, emitting an installable `<contentDir>/packs/` root whose `manifest.json` is merged (upserted) and whose pack directory contains the CSV fragment and assets.
- A duplicate id or mismatched header rejects the pack whole (core contract) and the content does not modify any base card row.

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `packs/manifest.json` + `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/{cards.csv,assets/}` + `packs/README.md`, mirroring `core/tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/`.
- Namespace card ids (`biz-ms-residential-…`, `evt-ms-residential-…`, `upg-ms-residential-…`, `stf-ms-residential-…`, `cs-ms-residential-…`) and pick distinct display names to avoid art-alias collisions.
- Add `"build:card-pack": "tsx ./core/scripts/build-card-pack.mjs --input packs"` to `package.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packs/manifest.json` — New pack catalogue entry.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/cards.csv` — New ~10-card residential fragment.
- `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` — New pack art assets.
- `packs/README.md` — New authoring/building/installing guide.
- `./package.json` — Add the `build:card-pack` wrapper.
- `core/tests/fixtures/reference-packs/main-street/` — Layout/oracle (read).

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: residential pack content & builder contract**.
- Art assets for the cards are produced by **Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage**.

## Deliverables

- The committed production pack source tree, the npm build wrapper, and a documented install path.

# Bespoke residential pack art & generator coverage

**Summary:** Produce bespoke, deterministic, licence-clean 1024×1024 source sprites for every residential pack card and extend the art-map generator so pack card names are mapped and resolve to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art in the regenerated `src/card-art-map.json`.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- One bespoke sprite per new pack card, committed under `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`.
- Art is project-generated and reproducible; base card art output must not regress.
- Small pack-art assets under `packs/main-street/main-street-residential-pack/assets/` are owned by the content child; this child owns the card-face source sprites and the generated map.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A committed, deterministic generator produces the pack card sprites (`src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`) reproducibly (identical input → byte-identical output) using the existing `sharp` dependency; the art is project-owned (CC0) and contains no third-party content.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is extended to include the production pack CSV fragment(s) in addition to `src/card-data.csv`, so pack card names are mapped and aliased.
- Regenerating `src/card-art-map.json` covers every new pack card with a valid 256×256 WebP bitmap entry resolving to a non-`Fallback` sprite.
- The runtime resolver (`resolveCardArtName`/`hasDedicatedCardArt`) and the static SVG generator resolve every pack card to the same dedicated sprite.
- Regeneration leaves the existing base-card aliases/art entries unchanged apart from the additive pack entries.

## Minimal Implementation

- New `src/scripts/generate-residential-pack-art.mjs`: deterministic SVG→PNG (or equivalent vector) art for the pack cards via `sharp`, with a fixed seed/palette per card.
- Parameterise the CSV inputs in `generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` so it reads the base CSV plus `packs/**/cards.csv`.
- Regenerate and commit `src/card-art-map.json` and the sprites.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/generate-residential-pack-art.mjs` — New deterministic sprite generator.
- `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` — New bespoke source sprites (one per new card).
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Include pack card rows.
- `src/card-art-map.json` — Regenerated art map covering the new cards.
- `src/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — Resolver (read).

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: residential pack art coverage**.
- Uses the card names/ids authored by **Production residential pack content & builder wrapper**.

## Deliverables

- Deterministic art generator, committed sprites, and a regenerated art map covering every pack card.

# Content-unlock pack entitlement gate

**Summary:** Compose Main Street's pack entitlement resolution so a `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack` unlock in the launcher's unified content-unlock store entitles the pack **in addition to** the existing Steam-DLC status, while an unowned pack stays locked and out of play.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Read side only: compose the content-unlock client into the `CardPackLoaderOptions.resolveEntitlement` seam used by `loadMainStreetCardPacks`.
- Do not change the core loader's default behaviour or other games' entitlement.
- Reuse the core `content-unlock-client` (`contentUnlockClientFromWindow`) and, where useful, the pure `DlcGate`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `loadMainStreetCardPacks` composes an entitlement resolver that reports a pack **unlocked** when a `dlc:<gameId>:<packId>` content unlock exists, in addition to the existing Steam-DLC status.
- With no content unlock the residential pack resolves **locked** with an actionable reason and its rows stay out of the merged pool; with the unlock it resolves **unlocked** and its rows merge.
- Only packs declared as content-unlock gated are affected; entitlement for every other pack and game is unchanged.
- The composition is total (never throws): a missing, throwing or malformed content-unlock bridge degrades to the Steam status / base content.
- The gating declaration is data-driven (a pack/manifest or game-config declaration), not a hard-coded pack title in logic.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an optional `contentUnlocks` client (defaulting to `contentUnlockClientFromWindow()`) and a composed `resolveEntitlement` in `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` (or a new focused `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` module).
- Determine which pack ids are content-unlock gated from an explicit declaration (proposed: an additive `entitlement` marker surfaced on `CardPackStatusRef`; record the final shape as an assumption if it differs).
- Extend `tests/main-street/MainStreetCardPacks.test.ts` seam coverage in the pipeline verification child.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — Compose content-unlock entitlement into the loader seam.
- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts` — New (optional) focused resolver.
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`, `core/src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` — Read/reuse.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — `resolveEntitlement` seam (read; additive ref shape only if required).

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.
- Blocks **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance** (the listing must render the locked → unlocked transition).

## Deliverables

- A total, data-driven content-unlock composition at the pack entitlement seam, with the gating declaration documented.
data.title: Content-unlock pack entitlement gate

# Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher

**Summary:** Add a config-driven, rule-scoped simulated purchase to the core launcher's unified content-unlock mechanism so a dev/QA affordance can unlock the residential pack's DLC target without collateral-unlocking other rewards (notably the itch.io golf reward).

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- Write path (main process + renderer read client) in the `./core` submodule; commit there and bump the submodule pointer in this work item.
- Keep the change additive and config-driven (no hard-coded game/DLC names in logic).
- Must not weaken the existing `steam-follow` self-attest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` gains a config rule whose target is `dlc:main-street:main-street-residential-pack`, triggered by a dev/QA `(platform, action)` pair resolved to a simulated-purchase verifier.
- `ActionRewardService.refresh` accepts an additive rule-scope filter and an explicit simulated-purchase signal, forwarded to `ActionVerificationRequest`; a scoped refresh evaluates only the named rule(s) and never self-attests unrelated rules.
- A `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (or equivalent) verifies **only** when a simulated purchase is explicitly requested, so a global `refresh({ attested: true })` cannot unlock the residential pack.
- The `contentUnlocks:refresh` IPC handler and preload bridge carry the scoped request, and the renderer `ContentUnlockClient` exposes a typed `refresh` call (the existing `isUnlocked`/`getUnlocks` API is unchanged).
- Tests prove a scoped residential purchase unlocks the residential DLC and does **not** unlock the configured `itchio-follow` golf reward, and that global attestation does not unlock the residential pack.
- The core change is committed to `./core` and the submodule bumped in the same work item; both commit hashes are recorded.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `ActionRewardRefreshOptions` (`ruleIds?`, `simulatePurchase?`) and `ActionVerificationRequest` (`simulatePurchase?`) in `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` / `action-verifiers.ts`.
- Add `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier` (id `simulated-purchase`) and register it in `initContentUnlocks` (`core/electron/main.ts`) with the config's verifier mapping.
- Normalise `ruleIds`/`simulatePurchase` in `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`; pass through `core/electron/preload.cjs`; add `refresh()` to `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts`.
- Add the rule + `verifiers.actions` entry to `core/electron/action-rewards.json` (validated against `core/electron/bonus-catalog.json`, where `main-street` is already registered).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/electron/action-rewards.json` — New residential-pack purchase rule + verifier mapping.
- `core/electron/action-rewards.ts` — Rule-scope filter + simulated-purchase signal.
- `core/electron/action-verifiers.ts` — `SimulatedPurchaseVerifier`.
- `core/electron/action-rewards-ipc.ts`, `core/electron/preload.cjs` — Scoped refresh transport.
- `core/src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — Typed `refresh`.
- `core/electron/main.ts` — Register the verifier.
- `core/tests/electron/**` — New/extended unit coverage.

## Dependencies

- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.
- Blocks **Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance** (the affordance calls the scoped purchase).

## Deliverables

- Committed core change + submodule bump, with scoping proven by tests.
data.title: Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher

# Card Packs listing simulated-purchase affordance

**Summary:** Add a dev/QA affordance in the in-game Card Packs panel that performs the scoped simulated purchase for the residential pack, refreshes the pack pool, and lets the player enable the newly unlocked pack.

**Parent:** MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY (Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import).

## Scope

- UI-only change in Main Street plus an additive action seam on the reusable core `CardPackListing`.
- No animation (honours reduced motion by construction); plays the standard UI SFX.
- Inert in a plain browser with no content-unlock bridge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Card Packs panel renders a simulated-purchase control on the **locked** residential pack row (additive `onPurchase`/row-action seam on `CardPackListing`); the control is only offered for content-unlock-gated packs.
- Activating it performs the scoped purchase through the renderer content-unlock client, re-runs pack discovery (`loadMainStreetCardPacks`/`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) and re-renders the listing, so the pack shows **unlocked** and is enable-able.
- Enabling the newly unlocked pack merges its rows and its cards deal in play; the enabled set persists as the new-game preference via the existing `applyEnabledMainStreetPacks` path.
- With no content-unlock bridge (plain browser) the affordance is a no-op and the listing still renders without error; the interaction plays `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.UI_CLICK`.
- Keeps SLL layout (no hard-coded pixel coordinates) and a browser test covers locked → purchase → unlocked → enabled.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add an optional `onPurchase` callback/row action to `core/src/ui/CardPackListing.ts`.
- Wire `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` `showCardPacksDialog` to call the scoped refresh, re-discover and update `listing.setResult(...)`.
- Add a Main Street helper (e.g. `purchaseMainStreetCardPack(packId)`) wrapping the content-unlock client refresh for testability.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `core/src/ui/CardPackListing.ts` — Additive purchase/row-action seam.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Simulated-purchase affordance in the Card Packs panel.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — Purchase + re-discovery helper.
- `tests/main-street/CardPackListing.browser.test.ts` — Pattern source (read).

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Content-unlock pack entitlement gate** and **Scoped simulated purchase in the core launcher**.
- Verified by **Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline**.

## Deliverables

- A dev/QA simulated-purchase affordance wired end-to-end from the listing to the unified unlock store.
